set.approach: From the Applebee or Kain Hut area, climb to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col and walk west over the upper Vowell Glacier, aiming for the crest of it beside Pigeon Spire on the north. Drop into the Pigeon-Howser Col, scramble down large boulders onto a steep loose slope, then go down the glacier beyond, skirting big crevasses and curving north toward the East Creek bivy site, which looks straight at the tower. All the west-face routes are reached through this col. Lower in the basin the way crosses talus and boulder fields with scattered cairns; find the scree gully leading up to the ridge, then scramble the ridge to the foot of the climb.
set.descent_text: The standard descent is a line of bolted rappel stations. The first group follows the north ridge toward Central Howser Tower, and the later ones angle toward the east ridge, down a gully, a steep northeast-facing buttress and short steps to the anchor above the bergschrund. A final rappel over the bergschrund lands on the Vowell Glacier, where low-angle snow allows walking off. Walk back across the glacier to the Applebee side. A stance can be hard to find in the dark, so descend with daylight and a rope long enough to reach each station.

review.notes: MP area page: col approach, East Creek bivy, rappel sequence from north ridge toward east ridge to bergschrund. Blog: scree gully/ridge to base, bergschrund, Vowell walk back. Rappel counts differ across pages (11, 12, 6) so no count given.

set.approach: Lake O'Hara is reached by bus or on foot; from the lake outlet cross the stream and turn left (north), or from the campground take the signed trail south to the stream and bridge. About 300-400 m along, an obvious avalanche path on the east side holds a faint cairned climbers' trail. Follow it uphill through the path, crossing a gully at the foot of a low cliff band (often snow-filled), then pass through a break in the band and switchback toward the toe of the ridge. Continue along the base of the wall to the crest. The start is a single bolt near the foot of a large chimney or corner just back from the crest, with small ledges for gearing up.
set.descent_text: From the top, follow a couple of cairns down to the rappel anchors and make several rappels to reach easy walking terrain. From there a climbers' trail runs along the side of the sub-peak and joins the tourist trail beside Lake O'Hara, which leads back to the bus stop area.

review.notes: Single readable source (MP route page) for approach and descent. Rappel count left out (one source). Grade/pitches match row.
